mouse microvascular endothelial but not large-vessel endothelial cells are responsive to bFGF and that this response involves a switch in the expression of urokinasetype plasminogen-activator.

mouse endothelial cells from aorta (large vessels) and heart and brain capillaries respond to bFGF in vitro and in a similar way to that reported for human endothelial cells, whereas cells from brain capillaries and heart capillares show a more pronounced angiogenic potential than cells from aorta.

the angiogenic basic FGF induces a pro-angiogenic phenotype in mouse microvascular endothelial but not in large-vessel endothelial cells, and that this effect is mediated, in part, by the induction of a profibrinolyic phenotype.

the characterization of the angiogenic phenotype of three different mouse endothelial cell types, namely, microvascular brain endothelial cells, microvascular heart endothelial cells, and aortic endothelial cells.
the role of angiogenesis in tumor growth and the mechanisms by which tumor cells stimulate the formation of new blood vessels.
the characterization of endothelial cells from mouse tissues and the evaluation of their response to angiogenic growth factors.

mouse endothelial cells respond differently to bFGF depending on their origin.
